c.tagline: Bangladesh's port city of hills, sea, and Mezban feasts.

taxi.fareNote: Metered taxis are rare; green CNG auto-rickshaws are the main street option and fares must be negotiated up front. App-based Uber and Pathao rides are cheaper and hassle-free.

emergency.note: 999 is Bangladesh's national emergency number connecting to police, fire, and ambulance; English-speaking operators are available.

avoid.reason: Petty crime; caution at night; the Chittagong Hill Tracts require permits

hood_desc: Chittagong's main commercial and business district, home to banks, corporate offices, the WWII Commonwealth War Cemetery, and many mid-to-upscale hotels; a convenient, well-connected base for business and first-time visitors.
A bustling central hub around GEC Circle known for shopping malls, restaurants, cafes, and lively evening crowds; suits travelers who want dining and retail within easy reach.
An affluent, leafy residential district on the hills near Foy's Lake, home to diplomats, quiet streets, and upscale homes; good for travelers wanting a calm, green, low-traffic area.

A coastal district at the mouth of the Karnaphuli River famous for Patenga Sea Beach, the naval base, and seaside food stalls; suits visitors wanting sea views and sunset promenades away from the dense core.

water.note: Tap water isn't safe to drink; stick to bottled or properly filtered water.

transit.hours: City buses and human haulers generally run from around 6:00 AM to 10:00 PM; late-night travel relies on CNG auto-rickshaws and ride-hailing apps.
transit.note: Chittagong has no metro or tram; public transport is a mix of local buses, human haulers (tempos), CNG auto-rickshaws, and rickshaws, supplemented by Uber and Pathao.
transit.pay: Bus and human-hauler fares are paid in cash to the conductor on board (typically 10-30 taka per ride); there is no rechargeable transit card system. CNG and rickshaw fares are negotiated in cash.

tip.r: Not expected; rounding up the bill or leaving 5-10% at upscale restaurants for good service is appreciated but not customary.

food.name: Mezbani beef (mezban gosht)
food.desc: Fiery bone-in beef curry cooked in vast pots for Chittagong's mezban feasts, heavy with mustard oil, black pepper and ground chilli. Eaten with white rice.

places.name: Mezzan Haile Ayun
places.note: The name most associated with mezbani beef in the city; rich, peppery and properly spicy.

places.name: Mejjainna Bari
places.note: Family restaurant serving a full mezban thali of beef, chanar dal, nola and rice at fair prices.

places.name: Tava Restaurant
places.note: Open since 1993; mezbani beef alongside its kababs and rumali roti.

food.name: Kala bhuna
food.desc: Beef slow-fried with onion, ginger and whole spice until almost black, dry and intensely aromatic. Chittagong's most copied dish.

places.name: Mezzan Haile Ayun
places.note: Dark, glossy kala bhuna that regulars rate as the benchmark version.

places.name: Mejjainna Bari
places.note: Serves kala bhuna with bhuna khichuri or rumali roti in a relaxed family setting.

places.name: Tava Restaurant
places.note: Long-running kitchen doing the dry-fried beef alongside beef achari.

food.name: Chanar dal with nola
food.desc: Split chickpea lentils cooked down with beef shank and marrow bone, the compulsory mezban partner to the beef and the reason guests fight over the pot.

places.name: Mejjainna Bari
places.note: Mezbani dal and nola are the house specialities, served as part of the set feast.

places.name: Mezzan Haile Ayun
places.note: Chanar dal here is thick with marrow and eaten with plain rice.

places.name: Kazir Dewri food street
places.note: Cluster of beef-and-rice canteens near the stadium doing cheap mezban-style plates.

food.name: Shutki (dried fish) bhorta and curry
food.desc: Sun-dried loitta or chhuri fish pounded with chilli, garlic and onion into a pungent bhorta, or curried with taro stems. Coastal Chittagong on a plate.

places.name: Asadganj dried fish market
places.note: South Asia's biggest shutki wholesale bazaar; stalls sell every grade of dried fish.

places.name: Mejjainna Bari
places.note: One of the easier sit-down places to try shutki bhorta without hunting the bazaars.

places.name: Riazuddin Bazar cookshops
places.note: Working-day canteens around the market serve shutki bhorta with rice and dal.

food.name: Chittagonian akhni biryani
food.desc: Local biryani cooked with beef or mutton, short-grain chinigura rice and a lighter, sourer spice mix than Dhaka kacchi, often finished with potato.

places.name: Mejjainna Bari
places.note: Akhni biriyani is a fixture on the menu and comes with borhani and salad.

places.name: Kazir Dewri food street
places.note: Row of biryani and kacchi houses that fill up after evening prayers.

places.name: Tava Restaurant
places.note: Dependable rice-and-kabab spot for biryani plates in the Zakir Hossain Road area.

food.name: Beef nolar roast and kabab
food.desc: Beef shank braised until the marrow slips out, or minced and skewered as shik kabab and eaten with paper-thin rumali roti.

places.name: Tava Restaurant
places.note: Best known locally for shik kabab and rumali roti since the early 1990s.

places.name: Mezzan Haile Ayun
places.note: Serves nola and beef shank cuts as part of the Chittagonian spread.

places.name: Kazir Dewri food street
places.note: Charcoal kabab counters running late into the night near the stadium.

food.name: Borhani
food.desc: Salty-spiced yoghurt drink with mustard, mint, green chilli and black salt, drunk to cut the fat of mezban beef and biryani. Non-alcoholic.

places.name: Mejjainna Bari
places.note: Borhani is served alongside the mezban thali and the akhni biriyani.

places.name: Mezzan Haile Ayun
places.note: The standard chaser for its peppery beef; ask for it cold.

places.name: Kazir Dewri food street
places.note: Biryani houses here bottle their own borhani by the glass.

food.name: Malai cha and sugarcane juice
food.desc: Thick milky tea skimmed with cream, or fresh-pressed sugarcane juice with lime and black salt from street carts. The city's everyday non-alcoholic pair.

places.name: Kazir Dewri food street
places.note: Tea stalls pour malai cha late into the evening beside the kabab counters.

places.name: Riazuddin Bazar
places.note: Sugarcane presses and tea stalls all along the market lanes.

places.name: Chatteswari Road tea stalls
places.note: Student and office crowd stop here for cream tea and snacks through the day.

landmarks: Patenga Sea Beach
Where the Karnaphuli River meets the Bay of Bengal, this lively beach is famous for stunning sunsets, ship-watching, and its buzzing evening food-stall atmosphere.
Ethnological Museum of Chittagong
A fascinating collection showcasing the traditional dress, crafts, and lifestyles of Bangladesh's diverse indigenous hill tribes, unique among the country's museums.
Foy's Lake
A scenic artificial lake ringed by hills and amusement parks, popular for boating, picnics, and panoramic views that make it a favorite family outing spot.
Chittagong War Cemetery
A beautifully maintained Commonwealth cemetery honoring Second World War soldiers, its rows of white headstones amid manicured lawns evoke quiet, moving reflection.
Zia Memorial Museum
Housed in the former Chittagong Circuit House, this museum commemorates President Ziaur Rahman and displays artifacts from a pivotal chapter of Bangladeshi history.
Chandanpura Shahi Jame Mosque (Masjid-e-Siraj ud-Daulah)
An eye-catching mosque famed for its ornate blue-and-gold onion domes and minarets, making it one of the most photographed buildings in the city.
Shah Amanat Bridge
A graceful cable-stayed bridge spanning the Karnaphuli River, its illuminated silhouette at night has become a modern symbol of Chittagong's skyline.
Chittagong Port
Bangladesh's principal seaport and a bustling maritime gateway, offering striking views of cargo ships and the Karnaphuli River's constant nautical activity.
Shrine of Bayazid Bostami
A revered Sufi shrine complex famed for its sacred pond of hundreds of black soft-shell turtles, drawing pilgrims and curious visitors alike.
Chattogram Zoo
A green, family-friendly retreat in the city center featuring a variety of native and exotic animals, popular with locals and visiting families alike.

train.note: Chattogram railway station on Station Road is the southern terminus of the metre-gauge eastern network, with intercity services such as the Sonar Bangla, Subarna and Mahanagar Provati reaching Dhaka in about 6 hours, the Paharika and Udayan running to Sylhet, and the Cox's Bazar Express using the line opened in December 2023. Tickets go on sale online at eticket.railway.gov.bd 10 days before departure and popular trains sell out within minutes, so book the moment the window opens or use a station counter or travel agent. Trains are cheaper and more relaxed than the buses but slower on the Dhaka run. There are no international trains from Chattogram - the three cross-border services to India (Maitree, Bandhan and Mitali) run from Dhaka and Khulna and have been suspended since July 2024, and the Myanmar border has no rail link.

bus.note: Private coaches leave from two clusters of company offices, one south of GEC Circle on CDA Avenue and one on Station Road near Hotel Golden Inn; Green Line, Shohagh, Saudia and Hanif run to Dhaka (6-8 hours) and Cox's Bazar (3-4 hours), while cheaper local buses to Cox's Bazar go from Cinema Palace bus station. Green Line has the only direct service to Sylhet, about 7-8 hours. Tickets are bought at the counters or online through Shohoz - https://www.shohoz.com/. No international coaches start in Chattogram: services to Kolkata, Agartala and Siliguri leave from Dhaka, and the land border with Myanmar is closed.

intl.to: Hatiya & Barishal (Bangladesh) - BIWTC launches leave Sadarghat, about 1 km south of the railway station
Sandwip & Kutubdia (Bangladesh) - small ferries and speedboats from the Kumira and Banshbaria ghats north of the city
intl.op: local launch operators — tickets at the ghat

ferry.note: BIWTC's launches and sea-trucks from Sadarghat are the only scheduled boats, running down the coast to Hatiya and onward towards Barishal for Dhaka; the longer runs are overnight, and cabins should be reserved at the BIWTC office a day or two ahead. Winter cruise ships have in the past sailed from Chattogram to Saint Martin's Island, but sailings to the island are now restricted by government order and depart from Cox's Bazar instead. Services thin out or stop altogether during the April-October monsoon and cyclone season. The port itself is a container and cargo facility with no international passenger sailings.

half.name: Sitakunda
half.blurb: A coastal hill area north of the city with Chandranath Hill's temple climb and the tidal beach at Guliakhali.

full.name: Cox's Bazar
full.blurb: The world's longest unbroken natural sea beach, stretching along the Bay of Bengal south of the city.

full.name: Rangamati
full.blurb: A hill-district town on Kaptai Lake, where boat trips reveal a hanging bridge, tribal villages and the Shuvolong Waterfall.

full.name: Bandarban
full.blurb: A mountainous district of the Chittagong Hill Tracts, with cloud-level viewpoints like Nilachal and tribal Buddhist monasteries.
